report.releaseDate: c. 21 Oct 2026 (Wyoming Gaming Commission, September 2026 Combined Wagering Activity Report; trade coverage 22–27 Oct 2026)
report.currency: USD (market reports in USD; tables in $m unless stated)
report.verdict: Wyoming is a sub-$30m-GGR, online-only, five-operator sportsbook market in which September 2026 handle fell 14.2% YoY to $23.4m (three NFL Sundays vs four, and a ~30% DraftKings retrenchment) while GGR rose 5.6% to $2.45m and state tax jumped 40% to $146.7k as promo deductions were cut. The real story for an operator is regulatory: a cheap ($100k/5-yr), uncapped licence and a 10%-of-net (≈6% of GGR) tax sit under a live 20% tax proposal, a 2027 felony sweepstakes ban and a legislature increasingly focused on the $2.5bn-handle historic-horse-racing machine market that dwarfs sports betting.
summary: **A small, online-only, five-operator sportsbook market that just posted its first YoY handle decline in a football month.** September 2026 online sports wagering (OSW) handle was $23,417,556, -14.2% YoY from $27.3m (Sep-25) but +49% MoM from $15.7m (Aug-26); it was still the second-best month of 2026 after March ($28.5m). The calendar matters: September 2026 contained three NFL Sundays versus four in September 2025.

**Revenue rose despite lower stakes because hold normalised.** GGR was $2.45m (+5.6% YoY from $2.32m) on a 10.5% hold versus an operator-unfriendly 8.5% a year earlier. GGR is gross win before promo deductions; it is not the tax base.

**State tax jumped 40% on a shrinking handle because operators cut promotional spend.** Taxable 'online sports wagering revenue' (handle excluding free/promo wagers, less payouts, less 0.25% federal excise) was $1,466,874 vs $1.05m, so tax at 10% was $146,687 (+40.2% YoY, +7.3% MoM). Trade analysis of the WGC report puts promotional deductions -32.4% YoY; our derived total deductions (promo + excise) fell ~23% to ~$0.98m, i.e. promo ≈3.9% of handle vs ≈4.4%. Effective tax on GGR: 6.0% (Sep-25: 4.5%).

**DraftKings' retrenchment accounts for the entire decline.** DK handle fell ~$4.7m to ~$11.1m (~-30% YoY), with share dropping from 57.8% to 47.3%, while the other four books added ~$0.8m combined. DK GGR held at $1.32m (~54% of state GGR, ~11.9% hold), consistent with it shedding low-margin, promo-driven volume rather than losing customers' wallet.

**Challengers are taking share.** FanDuel $6.5m handle (+7.9%, 27.9% share, tax $30,180 ≈2x YoY); BetMGM $3.1m (-4.7%, 13.1%); Fanatics $1.8m (+13.1%, 7.7%); Caesars $0.90m (+42.2%, 3.9%). Fanatics paid $279 of tax on $2,786 of taxable revenue — deductions wiped out virtually all of its win, i.e. it is still in promo-led acquisition mode.

**The market is still growing on a YTD basis.** Jan–Sep 2026 handle $177.4m (+9% YoY, implying ~$162.8m in 9M-25). FY2025: handle $234.5m, GGR $27.4m (+20% YoY, AGA citing WGC; Covers shows $27.25m, RG.org $25.9m — we use the WGC/AGA figure), tax $1.9m. Lifetime since the 1 Sep 2021 launch (LSR tally to mid-2026): handle ~$906m, GGR ~$96m, tax ~$6.0m — an effective 6.3% of GGR.

**Online is 100% of commercial sports betting.** Wyoming authorised online-only sports wagering (W.S. 9-24-101 et seq., HB 133 of 2021, signed 5 Apr 2021); there is no commercial retail channel. Tribal casinos on the Wind River Reservation offer on-site sportsbooks under compact and are outside WGC statistics (GGR n/a).

**Sports betting is a rounding error next to historic horse racing (HHR).** HHR terminal handle was $240m in September alone (+16% YoY vs $206.7m), more than 10x sports handle. FY2025 HHR handle $2.49bn (+18% vs $2.11bn), payouts $2.2bn, 1,314 active terminals across 46 approved locations, operator gross profit ~$180m after payouts and taxes (WGC director to legislators). Three licensees: Wyoming Horse Racing LLC, Wyoming Downs, 307 Horse Racing (March 2026 handle split $108.5m / $77.6m / $57.8m).

**Skill-based amusement games (SBAG) are the third pillar.** 4,115 machines generated $133.7m gross revenue in 2025 (vs ~$95m in 2024, +41%), taxed at 20% of net proceeds; $2.75m distributed to municipalities. Machines are capped at four per licensed location (bars, truck stops, fraternal halls).

**Licensing is open, cheap and long-dated.** Operator permit $100,000 initial and $50,000 renewal, each valid five years; vendor (supplier) permit $10,000 / $5,000 renewal, five years; statute requires the WGC to issue at least five operator permits and sets no cap. Applicants must already be licensed in at least three other US jurisdictions [per HB 133; not re-verified this session]. Minimum age 18.

**The tax regime is among the lowest in the US and fully promo-deductible.** 10% of net OSW revenue, remitted monthly; first $300,000 per year to the Department of Health for county problem-gambling programmes, balance to the General Fund. LSO told legislators in May 2026 that the average OSW rate in other states is 19% and no neighbouring state is below 10%.

**A doubling to 20% is the live fiscal threat.** In June 2025 the Select Committee on Capital Financing & Investments ordered draft bills to lift OSW tax from 10% to 20%, SBAG from 20% to 25% and pari-mutuel from 1.5% to 2.5%; the package died in September 2025 when House members blocked committee sponsorship after Sports Betting Alliance lobbying. The 2026 budget session saw no tax bill introduced (HB0171 on problem-gaming fund distribution was not even considered). Expect the 20% proposal to resurface for the January 2027 general session.

**Enforcement direction: a felony sweepstakes ban is heading to the 2027 session.** The legislature's Select Committee on Gaming (created 2025, renewed 2026) voted 9-0 in October 2026 to sponsor a bill making the operation of online sweepstakes games a felony, after an August 2026 draft that also swept in online casino games stalled on definitional doubts. WGC executive director Nick Larramendy warned that offshore iGaming/sweepstakes operators are using Wyoming LLCs as a front. A regulated iGaming bill (HB 162, 2025) failed and no 2026 iGaming measure advanced.

**Payments are app-native.** Debit/ACH/e-wallet funding is standard; Wyoming's OSW rules are notable for expressly permitting digital, crypto and virtual-currency account funding [widely reported at launch; not re-verified this session]. No cash/retail channel exists for commercial books.

**Responsible gambling and advertising rules are light-touch but tightening at the margin.** The $300k annual problem-gambling earmark is the main funding line (a 2026 proposal to add a further $300k from the industry was floated in committee); the WGC joined a national voluntary self-exclusion programme in December 2025; a May 2025 rule gives the WGC express power to exclude bettors who harass athletes. There is no state advertising code beyond the WGC rules and statute; age 18+ is among the lowest thresholds in the US.

**Local control is emerging as a constraint on land-based growth.** Casper City Council set a June 2026 hearing on a 180-day moratorium on new HHR establishments; the Select Committee on Gaming is studying local control, a statutory purse floor for live racing, responsible-gaming funding and prediction markets.

**Scale context.** Wyoming's $2.45m September GGR is ~0.2% of the US September total (~$1.08bn GGR on ~$12.5bn handle, RG.org tally). FY25 GGR equates to roughly $61 per adult (~$520 of handle per adult on ~450k adults) — healthy per-capita engagement in a tiny population.

**Read-through for an operator weighing entry.** Entry cost is trivial ($100k) and the tax is the lowest effective rate in the US, but the addressable prize is ~$27–30m GGR a year, 75% of which sits with DraftKings and FanDuel. A sixth B2C sportsbook realistically targets a 5–10% share (~$1.5–3m GGR) — sub-scale for a standalone P&L. The more interesting angles are B2B/platform supply (vendor permit $10k) to HHR/ADW licensees, or using Wyoming as a low-cost regulatory 'reference licence' — provided the operator already holds three other US licences. A move to 20% tax would cut net margin by ~3–4pp of GGR; the sweepstakes ban removes grey-market competition.

segments.name: Online sports betting — September 2026 performance and operator dynamics
segments.headline: Handle -14.2% to $23.4m on a three-Sunday September and a ~30% DraftKings pull-back; GGR +5.6% and tax +40% as promos were cut.
narrative: The WGC's September Combined Wagering Activity Report shows online sports wagering handle of $23,417,556, down 14.2% from $27.3m in September 2025 but up 49% from August's $15.7m. September 2025 was itself a record September (+19% YoY), and the 2026 NFL calendar delivered only three Sundays (13, 20, 27 Sep) against four a year earlier, so roughly a quarter of the football volume shifted into October. Even so, September was Wyoming's second-strongest month of 2026 behind March ($28.5m, March Madness), and nine-month handle of $177.4m is +9% YoY, so the underlying market is still expanding at high single digits rather than contracting.

Gross gaming revenue rose 5.6% to $2.45m because hold recovered to 10.5% from a bettor-friendly 8.5%. Hold has been volatile all year — 12.1% in January, ~7% in March (GGR only $2.0m on $28.5m handle), 14.3% in July, 11.5% in August — which is typical of a market this small, where a handful of parlay outcomes swing monthly results. Taxable net revenue (after free/promo wagers and the 0.25% federal excise) was $1,466,874 versus $1.05m, producing state tax of $146,687 (+40.2% YoY, +7.3% MoM). Our derived promo plus excise deductions were ~$0.98m (~40% of GGR; promo ≈3.9% of handle) versus ~$1.27m (≈4.4% of handle) a year earlier; trade analysis of the report quotes promotional deductions down 32.4%. Either way, the effective tax burden on GGR was only 6.0%, and the YoY tax jump is a promo-mix effect, not growth.

DraftKings explains the whole decline. Its handle fell by ~$4.7m to ~$11.1m (about -30%), taking its share from 57.8% to 47.3%, while FanDuel, BetMGM, Fanatics and Caesars grew by ~$0.8m combined. DraftKings' GGR nevertheless held at $1.32m — roughly 54% of state GGR on an ~11.9% hold — which reads as a deliberate retreat from promo-subsidised, low-margin volume (DraftKings had a 66.6% handle share in March). FanDuel took $6.5m (+7.9%, 27.9% share) and nearly doubled its tax payment to $30,180 (≈$0.30m taxable). BetMGM $3.1m (-4.7%, 13.1%) 'recovered' from a weaker summer. Fanatics $1.8m (+13.1%, 7.7%) booked just $2,786 of taxable revenue and $279 of tax after deductions — a market-entry promo profile. Caesars $0.90m (+42.2%, 3.9%) remains a distant fifth.

Structurally, Wyoming is a two-operator market with three sub-scale followers: DraftKings and FanDuel together hold ~75% of handle and probably >80% of GGR. Annual GGR of $27.4m (FY25) across five brands means the third-placed operator earns perhaps $2–3m a year before marketing. For an entrant, the data say the available share pool is the ~25% outside DK/FD, and that volume is being contested with promo spend that is itself tax-deductible — a modest advantage versus states that cap promo deductions.

Market guidance does not exist (the WGC publishes no forecasts). Our estimate: Q4-25 handle was ~$71.7m; with October 2026 carrying an extra NFL Sunday and the YTD trend at +9%, FY2026 handle of ~$250–255m (+7–9%) and GGR of ~$26–28m at a 10.5–11% hold are reasonable (estimates, not WGC figures). State OSW tax for FY26 should land near $1.6–1.9m depending on promo intensity.

segments.name: Licensing & tax regime
segments.headline: Uncapped, $100k five-year permits and a 10%-of-net tax (≈6% of GGR) — the cheapest regulated US entry ticket, but a 20% rate is on the legislative agenda.
narrative: Online sports wagering was authorised by HB 133 (2021), codified at W.S. 9-24-101 through 9-24-106, signed by Governor Mark Gordon on 5 April 2021; the first apps (DraftKings, BetMGM) went live on 1 September 2021 and the WGC administers the regime alongside pari-mutuel, HHR and skill-game licensing. The statute defines 'online sports wagering revenue' as 'the total of all wagers placed by patrons ... excluding the actual dollar value of free wagers and promotional play provided, minus all payments to patrons and minus any applicable federal excise taxes' — so the tax base is net revenue after promos and the 0.25% federal handle excise, with no cap on the deduction. That is why effective tax on GGR has run between 4.5% (Sep-25) and 7.6% (Aug-26) and averaged ~6.3% since launch ($6.0m tax on ~$96m GGR). Operators remit 10% monthly by the 15th; the first $300,000 collected each year goes to the Department of Health for county problem-gambling programmes and the remainder to the General Fund.

Permit economics are negligible by US standards. The commission charges $100,000 for an initial sports wagering operator permit and $50,000 for renewal, each valid five years; a sports wagering vendor permit (suppliers/platform providers) costs $10,000 initially and $5,000 on renewal, also five years. The statute obliges the WGC to issue at least five operator permits and imposes no maximum, so entry is not gated by auctions or market-access partnerships with land-based licensees — unusual for the US. The eligibility filter is instead experience: applicants must already hold sports wagering licences in at least three other US jurisdictions [HB 133 requirement as widely reported; not re-verified this session]. The LSO's May 2026 short report refers to six licensed operators; five are active in the September data, so a sixth permit holder may exist without a live product [unverified].

The tax debate is the key regulatory risk. In June 2025 the Select Committee on Capital Financing & Investments voted to draft bills doubling the OSW rate to 20%, lifting the SBAG net-proceeds tax from 20% to 25% (increment earmarked for highways) and raising pari-mutuel tax from 1.5% to 2.5% of handle, with the chair describing 20% as a 'placeholder' pending LSO fiscal notes. The Sports Betting Alliance argued higher rates push play offshore and worsen odds; in September 2025 the sponsorship vote failed on the House side and the committee adjourned early. The 2026 budget session produced no gaming tax bill — HB0171 (redistributing OSW tax for problem-gaming treatment, nine House sponsors) was not considered for introduction. But LSO's May 2026 briefing to the Select Committee on Gaming — average other-state OSW rate 19%, no neighbouring state below 10%, Wyoming having collected just $3.8m on ~$69m of revenue through mid-2025 — keeps the issue alive for the January 2027 general session.

Commercially, at 10%-of-net the state take is ~$0.6 per $100 of handle; at 20% it would be ~$1.2 per $100 — roughly 3–4pp of GGR off operator net margin given current promo levels, or more if promo deductibility were also curtailed (not currently proposed). Because Wyoming's GGR is ~0.2% of the US total, national operators would absorb a 20% rate without exiting; the pressure would instead fall on promo generosity and pricing, which is the lever an entrant would need to compete on.

segments.name: Historic horse racing, skill games, pari-mutuel, tribal & lottery — the land-based ecosystem
segments.headline: HHR terminals took $2.49bn in 2025 and $240m in September 2026 alone; the political and fiscal centre of gravity in Wyoming gaming is the machine floor, not the sportsbook app.
narrative: Historic horse racing — slot-style terminals whose outcomes are seeded from archived races, legally pari-mutuel — is Wyoming's dominant gaming product. The WGC's 2025 annual report (released May 2026) put HHR handle at $2.49bn, up from $2.11bn in 2024 (+18%), with $2.2bn returned to players, 1,314 active terminals across 46 approved locations and three licensees (Wyoming Horse Racing LLC, Wyoming Downs, 307 Horse Racing). The WGC director told legislators operators retain roughly $180m of gross profit after payouts and taxes, and that the state's 1.9% handle levy produced $24.9m for cities and counties (the 1% local share) — implying ~$47m of total HHR tax at the 1.9% rate (our estimate). In September 2026 HHR handle was $240m, +16% YoY versus $206.7m, more than ten times sports betting handle; March 2026 was $243.9m.

Handle is a misleading measure of HHR scale because recycled winnings inflate it — the director's own illustration to the committee was that $1 deposited, won up to $5 and replayed produces $6 of 'handle'. On a net-win basis HHR generates perhaps $290m a year (handle less payouts), still an order of magnitude larger than the $27m sportsbook GGR, and it is taxed on handle rather than win, which is why operators argue their effective burden is already ~1.9% of handle (≈16% of net win, our estimate). The committee is examining a statutory floor on the share of HHR revenue that must fund live-racing purses, and Casper (Natrona County, which received $2.89m of HHR distributions) set a June 2026 hearing on a 180-day moratorium on new HHR venues — the first sign of local saturation politics.

Skill-based amusement games are the second land-based pillar: 4,115 machines in bars, truck stops and fraternal halls generated $133.7m of gross revenue in 2025 (up from ~$95m), taxed at 20% of net proceeds (operator win after payouts; September 2024 example: $12.4m collected, $9.3m paid out, $3.1m net, ~$620k tax). Municipalities received $2.75m in 2025. The four-machine cap per location and the proposed 25% rate are the live regulatory questions; the industry (Cowboy Skill Games and others) has lobbied hard that a rise hits small businesses.

Live racing is small (one track active in a typical month; ~$155k handled by Wyoming Horse Racing LLC in September 2024), and advance-deposit wagering is reported in the same WGC activity report — DraftKings entered the Wyoming ADW market in 2026 with a trivial ~$21.7k monthly handle. Two tribes on the Wind River Reservation (Northern Arapaho: Wind River Hotel & Casino, Little Wind, 789; Eastern Shoshone: Shoshone Rose) operate Class III casinos under compact, including on-site sportsbooks; their GGR is not published (n/a). The Wyoming Lottery (WyoLotto) sells draw games only, with no instant tickets or iLottery; FY2026 sales were not retrievable this session (n/a).

For an operator the implication is that Wyoming's regulated money is in the HHR/SBAG channel, which is closed to new entrants in practice (three HHR licensees tied to racetrack permits; SBAG distributor licensing) but open to B2B supply: a $10k vendor permit covers platform and content supply, and HHR licensees' pivot to larger venues ('Horse Palace'-type proposals in Casper) creates demand for systems, cashless and loyalty technology.

blocks.heading: Skill games
blocks.takeaway: 4,115 skill-game machines generated $133.7m gross revenue in 2025 (up from ~$95m), taxed at 20% of net proceeds.
points: September 2024 example: $12.4m collected, $9.3m paid out, $3.1m net, ~$620k tax.
Municipalities received $2.75m in 2025.
Four-machine cap per location and proposed 25% rate are the live regulatory questions; Cowboy Skill Games and others lobbied that a rise hits small businesses.

blocks.heading: Racing, tribal, lottery
blocks.takeaway: Live racing, ADW, tribal casinos and WyoLotto are small or unpublished components of the ecosystem.
points: Live racing: one track active in a typical month; ~$155k handled by Wyoming Horse Racing LLC in September 2024.
DraftKings entered Wyoming ADW in 2026 with a trivial ~$21.7k monthly handle.
Northern Arapaho (Wind River Hotel & Casino, Little Wind, 789) and Eastern Shoshone (Shoshone Rose) operate Class III casinos including on-site sportsbooks; GGR not published (n/a).
WyoLotto sells draw games only, no instant tickets or iLottery; FY2026 sales not retrievable (n/a).

blocks.heading: Operator implication
blocks.takeaway: Regulated money sits in the HHR/SBAG channel, closed to new entrants in practice but open to B2B supply via a $10k vendor permit.
points: Three HHR licensees tied to racetrack permits; SBAG distributor licensing.
HHR licensees' pivot to larger venues ('Horse Palace'-type proposals in Casper) creates demand for systems, cashless and loyalty technology.

segments.name: Payments, responsible gambling, advertising & enforcement — and the legislative direction of travel
segments.headline: Light-touch RG and advertising rules, crypto-friendly funding, but a hardening line on grey-market sweepstakes/iGaming and a legislature hunting for revenue.
narrative: Account funding in Wyoming is app-native: debit card, ACH/online banking and e-wallets dominate, and the WGC's 2021 OSW rules were the first in the US to expressly allow 'digital, crypto and virtual currencies' as a funding method [widely reported at launch; rule text not re-verified this session]. In practice the five national operators use their standard US cashier stacks; the practical constraint is the absence of any cash or retail channel, which keeps the market fully KYC'd and geolocated but caps reach among unbanked or cash-preferring customers. Wyoming's small, dispersed population (under 600k) also makes customer acquisition cost per active high relative to lifetime value, which is the economic reason promo deductions matter so much to operator margins here.

Responsible-gambling architecture is minimal but being built out. The statutory earmark of the first $300,000 of OSW tax funds county problem-gambling treatment via the Department of Health; a May 2026 committee proposal would add a further $300,000 contribution from the industry, and HB0171 (2026) sought to re-route the distribution but was never introduced. In December 2025 the WGC announced Wyoming had joined a national voluntary self-exclusion programme, and in May 2025 it adopted rule amendments giving it express authority to exclude from the market any person who harasses an athlete. The minimum age of 18 (versus 21 in most states) and the absence of statutory deposit or advertising limits mean Wyoming is among the least restrictive US jurisdictions on the consumer-protection axis — a reputational rather than a commercial constraint for now.

Advertising is governed by general WGC rules and the statute rather than a bespoke code; there are no bans on bonus advertising, no affiliate licensing regime and no college-sports or in-stadium restrictions beyond federal/NCAA norms. The committee chair in September 2025 did criticise the sports betting industry's 'unhealthy marketing campaigns' against the tax bill, which signals that an operator-funded public campaign in a future tax fight could backfire politically.

Enforcement priority has shifted decisively to unlicensed online products. The Select Committee on Gaming — a 2025 task force renewed for 2026 and charged with studying wagering growth, local control, horse-racing and RG funding and prediction markets — requested in May 2026 a bill draft to prohibit iGaming and 'similar online activities' explicitly, after the WGC director described offshore operators using Wyoming LLCs as a legitimacy front. The August 2026 draft, which would have added online casino games and sweepstakes platforms to the professional-gambling definition, stalled on doubts about whether existing statute already covered them and about WGC capacity. In October 2026 the committee voted 9-0 to sponsor a narrower bill for the 2027 general session making operation of online sweepstakes games a felony; VGW told the committee it has offered sweepstakes games in Wyoming since 2012 and that the drafting would make Wyoming almost the only state to disallow free-entry models. Regulated iGaming, by contrast, has failed twice (HB 120, HB 162) and no 2026 bill advanced, so Wyoming remains sports-only online for the foreseeable future. Prediction markets (Kalshi-style event contracts) are on the committee's study list but no Wyoming action has been taken.

Net direction of travel: fiscal tightening (tax rate), definitional tightening (sweepstakes/iGaming), and local-control tightening on land-based expansion — but no appetite for new regulated verticals. For a licensed operator this is mildly positive on competition (grey-market removal) and negative on margin (tax); for a sweepstakes or offshore-facing brand it is an exit signal.

highlights.text: Lowest-cost regulated US entry: $100k operator permit for five years ($50k renewal), $10k vendor permit, no cap on permits and no land-based market-access tether — total licensing outlay for a decade is under $200k.

Lowest effective tax in the US: 10% of net revenue with uncapped promo and federal-excise deductions yields ~6% of GGR (Sep-26 6.0%; FY25 6.9%), giving an entrant promo headroom that is partly state-subsidised.
Market still growing high-single-digits: 9M-26 handle +9% to $177.4m after FY25 GGR +20% to $27.4m; per-adult GGR of ~$61 shows engaged customers despite a tiny population.

The leader is retreating: DraftKings' share fell from 57.8% to 47.3% in a year as it cut promo-driven volume, and the four challengers grew $0.8m combined — share is contestable for a well-funded product.
Grey-market clearance ahead: a 9-0 committee-sponsored felony ban on online sweepstakes for the 2027 session, plus WGC focus on offshore LLC fronts, removes untaxed competition for licensed books.

B2B optionality in the dominant channel: HHR ($2.49bn handle, 1,314 terminals, three licensees expanding into larger venues) and 4,115 skill games create demand for platform, cashless and loyalty supply under a $10k vendor permit.
Crypto-friendly funding rules and an 18+ age threshold widen the addressable base relative to 21+ states [funding rule not re-verified this session].

lowlights.text: Scale: ~$27m annual GGR, ~0.2% of US sports betting; a sixth brand realistically targets 5–10% share (~$1.5–3m GGR), sub-scale as a standalone P&L before marketing.

Concentration: DraftKings + FanDuel hold ~75% of handle and likely >80% of GGR; Caesars after five years has 3.9% share and Fanatics is paying $279 of monthly tax after promo deductions — evidence that challengers' economics are thin.

Tax-doubling risk: the 20% OSW rate (with SBAG 25% and pari-mutuel 2.5%) was drafted in June 2025, died on a procedural vote in September 2025 and is primed to return in the January 2027 general session; LSO has told legislators every neighbour taxes at ≥10% and the national average is 19%.

Hold volatility and calendar effects dominate monthly results: hold swung from ~7% (Mar-26) to 14.3% (Jul-26); September 2026 handle fell 14% largely because of one fewer NFL Sunday — budgeting on monthly data is unreliable.
Eligibility gate: applicants must already hold licences in at least three other US jurisdictions [per HB 133; not re-verified], so Wyoming cannot be a first US licence.

No product expansion path: regulated iGaming has failed twice, no 2026 bill advanced, and the Select Committee's instinct is to prohibit rather than regulate online casino-style products; sweepstakes/social casino business models face a felony ban.
Political optics: the committee chair publicly criticised industry 'marketing campaigns' against the tax bill; an operator seen to be lobbying aggressively risks hardening the legislature's stance.

Data transparency: the WGC publishes PDFs via Google Drive with no machine-readable series, and FY25 GGR is reported differently by AGA ($27.4m), Covers ($27.25m) and RG.org ($25.9m); operator-level net revenue is only partially disclosed.

forecast.intro: There is no official guidance for a market; the 'bridge' below is our view of how the key regulatory parameters and market size move from today's position to end-2027. The swing factor is the 2027 general session (January–March 2027): the Select Committee on Gaming will carry a felony sweepstakes-ban bill with 9-0 committee backing, and the Select Committee on Capital Financing & Investments, having briefed itself in May 2026 that Wyoming's 10% rate is roughly half the national average, is likely to re-file the 20% OSW / 25% SBAG / 2.5% pari-mutuel package that failed procedurally in September 2025. On the market side, September's -14% is calendar- and DraftKings-driven; underlying growth is high-single-digit and October 2026 (five NFL Sundays) should rebound.

bridge.change: Effective burden ~6% → ~12% of GGR if enacted (2027 session; probability ~40–50%, our view)

forecast.view: **Market:** we expect FY2026 handle of ~$250–255m (+7–9%) and GGR of ~$26–28m, with FY2027 growth slowing to mid-single digits as DraftKings' promo retrenchment and the loss of three-Sunday Septembers wash through; hold should settle around 10–11%. **Tax:** we assign a 40–50% probability that a 20% OSW rate passes in 2027 — the 2025 failure was procedural (House-side committee votes) rather than substantive, revenue pressure on the General Fund persists, and LSO's comparative data undercut the industry's argument; if enacted, state OSW tax roughly doubles to ~$3.5–4m a year on current promo levels and operator net margin falls 3–4pp of GGR, with promo deductibility the next target if revenue disappoints. **Regulation:** the sweepstakes ban is likely to pass; regulated iGaming will not; HHR will face a purse-floor mandate and growing municipal moratoria rather than state-level restriction; prediction markets will be studied, not legislated, in 2027. **Leverage for an entrant:** the only durable edge is product and pricing against DK/FD in a promo-deductible regime; we would not underwrite B2C entry on a standalone Wyoming case, but a B2B/vendor-permit strategy into HHR/ADW tech or a bolt-on to a multi-state footprint is defensible at the current tax rate and marginal at 20%.
watch: January–March 2027 Wyoming general session: re-filing and fate of the 20% OSW / 25% SBAG / 2.5% pari-mutuel tax package; any move to cap promotional deductions.

Passage and final scope of the felony online-sweepstakes bill (Select Committee on Gaming, 9-0 sponsorship, Oct-26) — whether 'similar online activities' language captures social casino, DFS pick'em or prediction markets.
DraftKings' share trajectory (57.8% → 47.3% in twelve months) and whether FanDuel's gains (27.9%) are promo-led — monthly WGC operator tables for Q4-26, which has five NFL Sundays in October.

Promo intensity as a share of handle (≈3.9% in Sep-26 vs ≈4.4% a year earlier) and Fanatics'/Caesars' taxable-revenue lines — the leading indicator of whether challengers can make money at 5–8% share.
HHR local-control actions (Casper moratorium outcome) and the purse-floor bill draft, which determine whether the land-based channel keeps compounding at ~18% a year.
WGC 2026 annual report (due ~May 2027): FY26 HHR handle, SBAG revenue, operator count and any reference to a sixth OSW permit holder.
Any WGC rulemaking on advertising, deposit limits or affiliate marketing, and any federal change to the 0.25% handle excise (deductible from the Wyoming base).

report.confidenceNote: Reporting currency USD; no FX conversion required. The WGC September 2026 Combined Wagering Activity Report is hosted as a Google Drive PDF and could not be parsed directly in this session; its headline figures (handle $23,417,556; GGR $2.45m; taxable revenue $1,466,874; tax $146,687; operator handles and shares) are corroborated across three independent secondary reads of the report (LegalSportsBetting.com, RG.org, BettingInWY.com) and the Gaming Intelligence lead. Derived figures (promo deductions, DraftKings handle, Sep-25 operator shares, Aug-26 tax, HHR tax at 1.9%, FY26 estimates) are marked ~ or 'estimate'. FY25 OSW GGR differs by source (AGA/WGC $27.4m; Covers $27.25m; RG.org $25.9m) — we use the WGC/AGA figure. Not re-verified this session and flagged in text: the ≥3-other-jurisdiction licensing requirement, the crypto/virtual-currency funding rule text, the exact name of the national self-exclusion programme joined in Dec-25, the LSO reference to six licensed operators, tribal casino GGR and WyoLotto sales (n/a).
